item.title: Homeland Security Paid $464 Million for Airplanes. Then It Parked Them.
item.description: The agency used a no-bid contract to buy 10 used jets, saying they were urgently needed for deportation flights. But the fleet has largely sat idle for months.
item.dc:creator: David A. Fahrenthold, Andrea Fuller, Julie Tate, Nicholas Nehamas and Hamed Aleaziz
item.media:credit: Kathleen Flynn for The New York Times
item.media:description: A Boeing 737 passenger jet purchased by the Department of Homeland Security parked last month at Chennault International Airport in Lake Charles, La.

item.title: Trump Administration Lets Parts of the National Firearms Act Lapse
item.description: The retreat by the Justice Department effectively allowed a pillar of the Prohibition-era National Firearms Act to lapse.
item.dc:creator: Chris Cameron
item.category: Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives
Brady Campaign to Prevent Gun Violence
item.media:credit: Erin Schaff for The New York Times
item.media:description: The popularity of gun suppressors, once a niche accessory, has skyrocketed.

item.title: New Yorkers Who Lost Insurance After Trump Cuts Face Hard Choices
item.description: New York State’s generous health plan for working-class people was hit hard by federal funding cuts. More than 400,000 people are now looking for new coverage or living without it.
item.dc:creator: Emma G. Fitzsimmons
item.media:credit: Katie Orlinsky for The New York Times
item.media:description: Health experts have warned that the number of uninsured New Yorkers will rise as people struggle to afford private plans after losing their low-cost, federally subsidized coverage.

item.title: ICE’s Plan to Give Officers Electric Stun Gloves, and a Siege on Palestinian Homes
item.description: Plus, health candy?
item.dc:creator: Tracy Mumford, Will Jarvis, Margaret Kadifa, Jake Lucas, Ian Stewart, David M. Halbfinger and Chico Harlan
item.media:credit: Jamie Kelter Davis for The New York Times
item.media:description: The Department of Homeland Security described planned gloves as a “de-escalation device,” but critics said they could encourage agents to use more force.

item.title: Russian Blockade of Major Ukrainian Ports Threatens Global Grain Supplies
item.description: The deadly strikes are part of a long-running maritime battle with Ukraine and echo battles over other key shipping routes around the world.
item.dc:creator: Marc Santora
item.media:description: A vessel struck off the coast of Odesa, Ukraine, last month. The Russian campaign has halted nearly all shipping in and out of the port.

item.title: Trump’s Plane Switch Ruse Pales in Comparison With Putin’s Secrecy
item.description: President Trump’s Air Force One subterfuge pales in comparison to the secrecy surrounding Russia’s president, whose fixation on security has reached new heights in recent years.
item.dc:creator: Anton Troianovski
item.media:description: A Russian state media photo of President Vladimir Putin in his office in the Kremlin last month. The secrecy around Mr. Putin’s movements means journalists have resorted to tracking his activity by assessing the wilting of the plants in his office.

item.title: Putin Visits Islands Seized From Japan in World War II, Angering Tokyo
item.description: Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi of Japan has been a public critic of Mr. Putin, who has denounced her country’s sanctions against Russia over the Ukraine war.
item.dc:creator: Javier C. Hernández and Paul Sonne
item.media:credit: Gavriil Grigorov/Sputnik, via Agence France-Presse — Getty Images
item.media:description: A Russian state media photo released on Thursday showed President Vladimir V. Putin of Russia visiting a contested island.

item.title: Inside the Democratic Socialists of America’s Audacious Quest for Power
item.description: Democratic Socialists are capturing more votes than ever before — even as they run up against the limits of their appeal.
item.dc:creator: Charles Homans

item.title: In This State, an Intense Fight in the G.O.P. for Control of the Right
item.description: Wyoming, one of the most conservative states, has a legislature divided between a hard-right House and a merely right Senate. Ultraconservatives want a complete takeover in the Aug. 18 primaries.
item.dc:creator: David W. Chen and Will Warasila
item.media:credit: Will Warasila for The New York Times

item.title: How Thanksgiving Became Political: Francesca Hong’s Tweets Explained
item.description: Ahead of Wisconsin’s Democratic primary for governor, a past tweet by the assemblywoman that called for the holiday to be canceled was resurfaced.
item.dc:creator: Alisha Haridasani Gupta
item.media:description: In recent years, many schools have been rethinking how they teach students about Thanksgiving.

item.title: Luigi Mangione, Facing Stalking Charges in Federal Court, Is Expected to Plead Guilty
item.description: Mr. Mangione faces stalking charges resulting in the death of an executive in Manhattan. Mr. Mangione could always change his mind at the last minute. A separate murder trial is set to begin next month.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Weiser, Devlin Barrett and Hurubie Meko
item.media:credit: Pool photo by David Dee Delgado
item.media:description: If Luigi Mangione pleads guilty, his lawyers seem certain to seek a dismissal of his state charges on double jeopardy grounds.

item.title: How Bob Iger and Joshua Kushner’s Bromance Led Them to Lakers
item.description: Bob Iger, the former chief executive of Disney, and Josh Kushner, the venture capitalist, are buying the Los Angeles Lakers. Their wives set them up.
item.dc:creator: Brooks Barnes and Tania Ganguli
item.media:description: From left, the N.B.A.’s commissioner, Adam Silver, joined Joshua Kushner and Bob Iger at the 2025 U.S. Open tennis tournament.

item.title: In a Chinese Leader’s Death, Mourning for a More Hopeful Time
item.description: Tributes for former Premier Zhu Rongji reflect nostalgia for an era when China was opening to the world and the future seemed more prosperous and hopeful.
item.dc:creator: Li Yuan
item.media:description: Former Premier Zhu Rongji of China died on Wednesday. He was memorialized in Beijing.

item.title: How China Remembers Zhu Rongji, the Premier Who Spoke His Mind
item.description: Tributes to the former premier recalled his spirited style and his efforts to integrate China into global commerce, in contrast with the rigidity of the Xi era.
item.dc:creator: Chris Buckley
item.media:description: The official obituary of Zhu Rongji, at a newsstand in Beijing on Thursday.

item.title: Europe Is Once Again In the Grip of Extreme Heat

item.title: ‘An English Summer Is Not the Same Anymore’

item.dc:creator: Lynsey Chutel

item.title: Effects of Record-Breaking El Niño Are Happening on 3 Continents

item.dc:creator: Raymond Zhong and Chico Harlan

item.title: Outdoor Dining Is Expected to Resume Year-Round in New York City
item.description: The City Council is poised to approve a package of bills loosening some restrictions on roadway dining structures, which became ubiquitous during the pandemic.
item.dc:creator: Dana Rubinstein and Claire Fahy
item.media:credit: Marissa Alper for The New York Times
item.media:description: New York City’s outdoor dining program helped keep the restaurant industry afloat during the Covid pandemic, but also drew complaints about poorly maintained sheds, prompting the city to tighten regulations.
